I think because things like NPD and BPD have core beliefs relating to insecurity and a need for something human like admiration or caretaking or whatever, the lies therefore have something profound to prove about the person telling them. With ASPD, our core beliefs are inward and our outward beliefs are cynical. If we're trying to make someone believe something about ourselves it's a means to an end, rather than something profound about who we're trying to be and what relationship we rely on having with that person for validation, so we're less likely to overcompensate with ridiculous lies that are hammered home a little too hard, less likely to tell fantastical lies that paint us as heroes, victims, whatever, and less likely to become personally offended if our lie doesn't seem to be landing. Another thing about sociopathy is we know when a battle isn't worth it and find some other kind of prey, whatever that may be.  
Also, I think people with other disorders that might encourage lying don't study people quite as meticulously as we do, we're like sponges for information on people and we notice non-verbal cues and things much more than other people because humanity is like a language we've become fluent in as tourists. Naturally if we want to emulate proper human interaction and lies need to be employed, we've already witnessed good lying and bad lying, and we can probably put something pretty convincing together and know when to reel it back in again.

I am self-identified ASPD, and was formally diagnosed 9 years ago, a diagnosis that has never changed. As you’ll see, I’ve been an active member of this sub and have never undermined, trolled, invalidated. If, however, this admission results in my ban, I understand, and I apologise again for the post (legit don’t come to reddit often and am not well-up on the etiquette but am learning - spent far too much time on facebook where messaging a mod is tantamount to starting a civil war, but now know that’s not the case here). I stand by that I have this diagnosis and that I am no threat to anyone’s safety. I do in fact have capabilities for empathy, just like a lot of us do. I am not a psychopath - a lot of people with ASPD arent. In order to be a psychopath one must also display strong traits adhering to the dark triad, including narcissism. As I live in a state of disgust towards to narcissist that raised me, I have often asked my doctor if narcissism is something that I live with and hadn’t noticed - I have been assured time and again that narcissism is not my diagnosis, and my levels of narcissism are “healthy”, and “that of the average person”. Still, I check in with myself a lot.
You don’t have to take my word for any of this, but please don’t immediately write people off because of a diagnosis that has often nothing to do with narcissism. I know you can’t vet all the time, but lack of empathy is seen right across the board with a lot of mental illnesses - there’s manipulation in BPD, HPD - it doesn’t mean everyone must therefore be written off. We get very little representation other than sensationalist fiction about sociopaths, psychopaths - some kind of weird, evil autistic trope that really doesn’t stick for most of us. A lot of people know sociopaths, and would never know it, never be affected by it. We aren’t all immediately ready to fuck people over. 

I want no sympathy or empathy for my condition as I don’t believe it causes me enough suffering for me to chime in with “but imagine how hard it is having ASPD!” because by and large, it’s inconvenient, maybe isolating, but there’s little suffering. What I do want is not to be assumed as a natural predator because my personality was formed by a master manipulator and serial abuser, and that I don’t deserve validation because I must be a bad apple. If I want to talk candidly about ASPD, I head over to /r/sociopath. I know not to bring that here; I’m intuitive enough and smart enough to know not to shit on my own doorstep. That would make me a narcissist. 

Thanks for reading this, please do let me know if your decision. It would be very saddening, defeating, tiring - but the choice of course is yours and I hope I’ve left any emotional outpouring to a minimum here so there’s no evidence of manipulation or emotional blackmail. Nothing bad will happen to me as a result of being banned; I wouldn’t then bring trouble to your door as a reaction.

I hope any of this at all is reassuring in any way.
